name: reply-layout
what: Gives every reply the same shape: a title line, the answer, then Choices and To do, so a busy person can skim it.
look_for: The title line with name and time, and the Choices and To do lists at the end.
example: A reply that ends with one choice, its recommended option starred.

name: prompt-relay
what: Lets one Claude write a prompt for another, framed with a code, for a person to carry between threads.
look_for: A framed prompt with a four-digit code, and its answer carried back.
example: A price question sent from the writer to the researcher and answered.

name: decision-log
what: Records each settled decision with a number, so later replies can cite it instead of repeating it.
look_for: Codes like D-001 in replies, each pointing at one settled choice.
example: The pledge price, recorded once and cited from then on.

name: visual-picks
what: Shows options as pictures or small pages to look at and compare before picking.
look_for: A reply with pictures side by side and a pick to make.
example: Three card-back sketches, one of them recommended.

name: team-identities
what: Gives every Claude a name, an emoji, a role and pronouns, so a person always knows who is talking.
look_for: The emoji and name in every title line, the same across threads.
example: The bookkeeper and the tester, each with their own mark.

name: run-steps
what: Writes steps a person runs themselves in strict order, each with a check to confirm it worked.
look_for: Numbered steps, each ending in a Check line.
example: Fixing a download on the studio site, one step at a time.

name: second-look
what: Reviews another Claude's plan or draft and reports numbered findings, most serious first.
look_for: A short list of findings, each with what to change.
example: A review of the backer update calendar.

name: rough-notes
what: A safe place for a person's half-formed notes, tidied without losing anything.
look_for: Messy notes in, a clean version out, with nothing acted on yet.
example: Character ideas for a game night, sorted into three sheets.
